name: leads-out-of-area
about: Earlier ads drew many leads from too far away; the plan should say where the job is.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: A small fleet where dispatch knows your name

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.
Of 46 of our ad leads in the last 28 days, 40 were called and 27 were reached.
19 of 46 of our ad leads in the last 28 days were closed as: out of area.
4 of 46 of our ad leads in the last 28 days were closed as: not interested.

output.audience: Class A flatbed drivers who meet the experience the opening asks for and live along its Midwest lanes. They likely run regional or longer for a bigger fleet now. They would stop for a clear pay per mile, weekly home time and a truck that stays theirs.

angles.idea: Say plainly where the lanes run and what the opening requires, so a driver outside the Midwest knows it is not for them.
angles.proof: The job is Class A regional flatbed on Midwest lanes, with a stated experience requirement.
angles.why: Out of area was the largest reason earlier leads were closed. Stating the lanes and the requirement up front should filter before the form, though no hook has been measured yet.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile, shown over a loaded flatbed moving on a Midwest highway.
angles.proof: The opening states its pay per mile for flatbed work on Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Pay per mile is the most concrete fact of the job and easy to compare. No earlier ad result by hook is on the sheet, so this is untested.

angles.idea: Lead with being home weekly, pictured as a driver arriving on their own street in a Midwest town.
angles.proof: The opening offers home weekly on regional Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Weekly home time speaks to drivers who are out longer now. Naming the Midwest in the line keeps the appeal from pulling more out-of-area leads.

angles.idea: Lead with the assigned truck: the same flatbed rig waiting for the same driver, shown parked and ready.
angles.proof: The job comes with an assigned truck and is flatbed work.
angles.why: An assigned truck matters to experienced flatbed drivers and fits a small fleet. Nothing has been measured for this hook, so treat it as a test.

angles.idea: Set out the job's terms as a plain list on a plain background, closing on the small fleet where dispatch knows your name.
angles.proof: Pay per mile, home weekly, the retirement plan and the fleet's own description are all stated job facts.
angles.why: Some earlier leads were not interested when called. Showing the terms before the form lets drivers decide earlier. This is untested.
